Moniepoint Microfinance Bank says eligible customers can now check their status and access the Federal Government’s ₦50,000 emergency relief support through its Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) channel. The bank said in a statement issued on Wednesday that “customers could dial *5573*27# from their registered phone numbers and select the option to check their eligibility for the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI).” It said customers confirmed as beneficiaries would be guided through the steps to accept the support and receive the funds into their Moniepoint accounts at no additional cost. The intervention, led by the Federal Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, is designed to provide direct financial assistance to vulnerable households to help them meet essential needs amid prevailing economic pressures. On Tuesday, PUNCH Online reported that that FG had begun payment to eligible Nigerians. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The bank noted that the programme was being implemented in phases across the country, adding that not all customers would qualify or be selected at the same time. 74% of Nigerian tech startups maintain US ties – Report ICYMI: How FG selects beneficiaries for N50,000 relief FG’s N50,000 relief: OPay explains eligibility, warns against scams What moniepoint customers should know? Babatunde Olofin, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank, said the “bank was pleased to support eligible customers in receiving assistance under the government initiative.” Olofin said Moniepoint would deploy its technology and financial infrastructure to make the process accessible, seamless and secure. He urged “customers to use only the bank’s official USSD channel when checking their eligibility or accessing the funds.” He added that the process required “no additional payment, documentation or third-party intervention.” The bank also advised customers with enquiries to contact its customer service team or the NERSI helpdesk. Moniepoint said its nationwide network of financial services infrastructure, including Point-of-Sale terminals across the country’s 774 local government areas, would support efforts to extend access to the intervention.
